spikes.question: does the destination CONTRACT need a USDC trustline for the mint?
spikes.status: answered-by-mechanism + open-by-transaction (the mechanism: CCTP mints to CctpForwarder - a CONTRACT - on every inbound transfer today, so contract-side balance creation without a user-style trustline is the protocol's own happy path; whether an ARBITRARY contract (SpikeGate) needs anything extra is exactly what S1's claim will print)
spikes.answer: user-side accounts DO need a trustline before burn (UI gate stays); contract-side: answered by the S1 claim's balance read
evidence: spike-notes.md doc section; CctpForwarder flow description

spikes.question: soulbound NFT: standard or minimal bespoke
spikes.status: answered (decision at F3, with a test, as promised)
spikes.answer: minimal home-grown soulbound proof: the contract simply has no transfer, no approve, no burn_of; a transfer attempt is an unknown-function error. OpenZeppelin-Stellar was weighed and refused: pulling a transferable NFT base in and disabling parts of it would leave dead doors in the bytecode, while the directive asks for functions that are not there at all.
evidence: cargo test -p gate_claim --lib test::the_proof_is_soulbound_because_there_is_nothing_to_call (try_invoke_contract of `transfer` returns Err)
